forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Bracknell Forest Cabinet commits £6.764m of education capital grants to 25 more specialist school places
news_drafts.lead:
Bracknell Forest's Cabinet on 13 October was asked to approve spending £6.764m of education capital grant funding (money for things that last, such as buildings) on specialist provision for children with special educational needs and disabilities. The sum is made up of £5.051m of high needs place capital, £1.285m of basic needs funding, £75.8k from the Special Provision Capital Fund and £351.4k left over from earlier allocations. The paper says the council is "using the Education Capital grant funding £6,764m that is currently available".

The money would pay for projects across several school sites. By September 2027 they would create 15 more Specialist Base places and 10 more Special School places. The full programme aims for 95 Specialist Base places and 78 Special School places by September 2029.

The papers link the building work to two other matters. A 2025 inspection of the local area's special educational needs services identified a lack of local specialist provision as "an area of weakness", and the area was challenged to increase it, "something the proposed schemes will support". The report also says successful delivery of the local SEND Reform Plan is a requirement for the council to access the High Needs Stability Grant, which "will write off 90% of the accumulated debt against expenditure in the High Needs Block", the part of school funding for children with these needs. The paper does not give the size of that debt in the material reviewed.

findings.paper_title: For Cabinet - SEND Reform Sufficiency Capital Programme - Report Final (16.09.26) (002)
findings.headline: Capital programme addresses 2025 SEND inspection weakness regarding lack of specialist provision
findings.detail: The 2025 SEND Inspection identified a lack of local specialist provision as a weakness. The proposed capital schemes are identified as supporting the council's commitment to increase specialist provision in response to this inspection finding.
findings.matters: Demonstrates governance issue requiring capital remediation; continuation of inspection weakness could have ongoing regulatory consequences.
findings.quote: The 2025 SEND Inspection of Bracknell Forest local area identified a lack of local specialist provision as an area of weakness, and the local area was challenged to increase the amount of provision, something the proposed schemes will support.

findings.paper_title: For Cabinet - SEND Reform Sufficiency Capital Programme - Report Final (16.09.26) (002)
findings.headline: Successful SEND Reform Plan delivery is requirement for accessing High Needs Stability Grant providing 90% debt relief
findings.detail: The paper states that successful delivery of the local area SEND Reform Plan is a requirement to access the High Needs Stability Grant, which would write off 90% of accumulated debt in the High Needs Block. The capital projects are described as essential to meeting these SEND Reform commitments, creating direct linkage between capital programme delivery and major debt relief funding.
findings.matters: Represents significant contingent debt relief conditional on capital programme delivery; failure to deliver carries revenue risk for the council's budget position.
findings.figures: 90% debt relief on accumulated High Needs Block debt (total debt amount not specified)
findings.quote: Successful delivery of the local area SEND Reform Plan is a requirement for the Council to access the High Needs Stability Grant which will write off 90% of the accumulated debt against expenditure in the High Needs Block.

findings.paper_title: For Cabinet - SEND Reform Sufficiency Capital Programme - Report Final (16.09.26) (002)
findings.headline: College Hall asset sale deferred; £0.5m grant substituted to replace lost capital receipt
findings.detail: The council is deferring the planned sale of the College Hall site pending review of its potential permanent use for SEND purposes. This requires using £0.5m of available grant funding to replace the anticipated capital receipt originally earmarked for the Hawthorn Academy site development currently underway.
findings.matters: Represents change to anticipated capital receipts position and substitution of grant for receipt-based funding for concurrent capital schemes.
findings.quote: The sale of the College Hall site is put on hold pending a detailed review of the potential use of the site for permanent SEND purposes, noting that this will require use of £0.5m of available grant to replace the expected capital receipt in support of the Hawthorne Academy site development which is currently underway.

findings.paper_title: For Cabinet - SEND Reform Sufficiency Capital Programme - Report Final (16.09.26) (002)
findings.headline: Kings Academy project contingent on April 2027 DfE funding decision or other project underspends
findings.detail: The council can currently fund The Pines, Great Hollands, Mainstream Adaptations, and CDC redevelopment with available grant. Kings Academy Easthampstead Park is contingent on additional funding from the DfE in April 2027 or on underspends in other projects, creating a conditional element to full programme delivery.
findings.matters: Demonstrates funding constraints within the capital programme and creates delivery dependencies on future DfE allocation decisions.
findings.figures: Kings Academy contingent; four other projects fully funded from current £6.764m allocation
findings.quote: all projects can be delivered except King's Academy Easthampstead Park within existing grant residual funds. This project will only commence if additional capital grant funding is received from the DfE in April 2027 or if there is an underspend on any of the other projects included in the list.

findings.paper_title: For Cabinet - SEND Reform Sufficiency Capital Programme - Report Final (16.09.26) (002)
findings.headline: Cabinet approves £6.764m education capital grant funding for SEND provision projects
findings.detail: The council is deploying the full available education capital grant funding, comprised of £5.051m High Needs Place Capital Allocation plus other allocations, to fund specialist education provision across multiple school sites. These funds will create 15 additional Specialist Base places and 10 Special School places by September 2027, with the full programme targeting 95 Specialist Base and 78 Special School places by September 2029.
findings.matters: Represents deployment of significant education grant funding and a major capital commitment to addressing SEND sufficiency.
findings.figures: £6.764m total (£5.051m High Needs Place Capital; £1.285m Basic Needs; £75.8k Special Provision Capital Fund; £351.4k residual)
findings.quote: using the Education Capital grant funding £6,764m that is currently available

daily_post.headline: Pension liability increased significantly and is creating ongoing revenue pressure
daily_post.lead: Growing pension deficits create unpredictable revenue pressures and reduce the stability of financial forecasts that lenders rely on when assessing creditworthiness and repayment capacity.
